newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Senator says currently against Telstra sale.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Senator says currently against Telstra sale.

text.p: Australian Independent Senator Brian Harradine said on Monday he would vote against the one-third sale of telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp if the Senate voted on it today.
When asked if the bill would get his support this week Harradine said: "If it was to be voted on today it wouldn't."
But he did not commit himself to a final position.

"One would be rather unintelligent to do that because if, as I said, the government came good with all of the matters that I put forward on behalf of my state then one would be rather silly to oppose it," he told the Australian Broadcasting Corp Radio.
Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday he was still negotiating with Harradine and fellow Independent Mal Colston over the Telstra legislation.
The government needs the support of Harradine and Colston to pass the legislation in the non-government dominated upper house, the Senate.
The Labor opposition, the Australian Democrats and the Greens minor party are all opposed to the sale.
The conservative Liberal-National government plans to raise A$8 billion from the partial sale of Telstra, with A$1 billion earmarked for an environment package.
